docs.title: Home
docs.text:
🔌 immundapter – Lightweight R Adapters for Immune Repertoire Tools

Documentation | Ecosystem

Analyze ImmunData objects or immune receptor files with external tools, read result tables to R, and add the results as annotations to ImmunData objects.

docs.title: Supported tools
docs.text: Tool Input Result R help tcrdist3 ImmunData or a receptor table T-cell receptor distances and clusters ?tool_tcrdist3 ImmGLIPH ImmunData with TRB receptors Groups of similar TRB receptors ?tool_immgliph IgBLAST FASTA with optional annotations Germline gene calls ?tool_igblast RAxML-NG ImmunData with aligned B-cell receptor sequences Phylogenetic trees by family ?tool_raxml_ng VDJdb ImmunData Antigen specificity annotations ?data_vdjdb

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use R 4.1 or later.

install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("immunomind/immundapter")

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Print the tcrdist3 setup commands in R.
tool <- immundapter::tool_tcrdist3()
tool$help()

  1. Run the setup commands in your terminal.

  2. Cluster the T-cell receptors in the bundled example.

input <- system.file(
  "extdata", "tcrdist3", "tcr-cluster-simple.tsv",
  package = "immundapter", mustWork = TRUE
)
run <- tool$run(input, output_dir = tempdir())
  1. Read the cluster table.
dplyr::collect(run$results()$clusters)

docs.title: Results folder
docs.text: immundapter::set_output_dir() command saves a default folder for tools to read and write results from and to.

docs.title: VDJdb data source
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text: VDJdb is a reference database of T-cell receptors with known antigen specificities. data_vdjdb() manages a local copy of the slim VDJdb table and can add matching VDJdb records to immundata::ImmunData.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: data_vdjdb(output_dir = immundapter_data_path("data"))

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: output_dir Directory used to store VDJdb. Defaults to the data subdirectory of IMMUNDAPTER_DATA when set, or of tools::R_user_dir(“immundapter”, “cache”) otherwise.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: A VDJdb data source.

docs.title: Input and output
docs.text:
data \<- data_vdjdb() gives access to these commands:

  • data$download(): Print the download command and destination without downloading anything.
  • data$download(execute = TRUE): Download the latest VDJdb release. Use force = TRUE to replace an existing copy.
  • data$check(): Report whether VDJdb has been downloaded.
  • data$load(): Return the VDJdb table. The table stays on disk until you use dplyr::collect(). Use data$load(output = “df”) to return a base R data frame instead.
  • data$annotate(idata): Match receptors in an ImmunData dataset to VDJdb and return a new dataset with VDJdb columns. By default, matching uses CDR3 amino-acid sequence and receptor locus.
  • data$citation(): Return the VDJdb publication as an R citation.

For the default matching, ImmunData must contain junction_aa and locus. These are matched to the VDJdb columns cdr3 and gene: c(junction_aa = “cdr3”, locus = “gene”). Use the by argument to choose different matching columns. Added VDJdb columns start with vdjdb_, which makes them easy to distinguish from the original columns.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: VDJdb database

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immundapter")


data <- data_vdjdb(output_dir = tempfile("vdjdb-cache-"))

# First call: print instructions. Second call: perform the download.
data$download()
data$download(execute = TRUE)
data$check()

vdjdb_table <- data$load()
dplyr::collect(vdjdb_table)

input_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "tcrdist3", "tcr-cluster-simple.tsv",
  package = "immundapter"
)
idata <- immundata::read_repertoires(
  path = input_file,
  schema = immundata::make_receptor_schema(
    features = c("v_call", "j_call", "junction_aa"), chains = "TRB"
  ),
  barcode_col = "cell_id", locus_col = "locus",
  umi_col = "duplicate_count",
  output_folder = tempfile("vdjdb-immundata-")
)
annotated_idata <- data$annotate(idata)

docs.title: Group similar T-cell receptors with ImmGLIPH
Description
docs.text:
ImmGLIPH groups T-cell receptor beta chains that share sequence patterns and may recognize related antigens. The analysis uses CDR3 amino-acid sequences and can also use V genes, donor names, HLA types, and clone counts.

ImmGliphToolConfig stores the validated settings for an ImmGLIPH analysis. It contains no repertoire data and no results. Create it with conf_immgliph() and pass it to tool_immgliph().

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
conf_immgliph(
  method = "gliph2",
  reference = "human_v2.0_CD48",
  cdr3_col = "junction_aa",
  v_gene_col = NULL,
  patient_col = NULL,
  hla_col = NULL,
  counts_col = NULL,
  n_cores = 1L,
  seed = NULL,
  run_args = list()
)

tool_immgliph(config = conf_immgliph())

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: method ImmGLIPH analysis preset: “gliph2”, “gliph1”, or “custom”. reference Name of the reference repertoire included with ImmGLIPH. cdr3_col Name of the column containing TRB CDR3 amino-acid sequences. v_gene_col Optional name of the TRB V-gene column. patient_col Optional name of the donor or sample column. hla_col Optional name of the HLA column. counts_col Optional name of the clone-count column. n_cores Positive integer number of CPU cores used by ImmGLIPH. seed Optional integer random seed for a reproducible ImmGLIPH run. run_args Additional named arguments passed to immGLIPH::runGLIPH(). Use this only for advanced ImmGLIPH settings. Arguments controlled by immundapter cannot be changed here. config An ImmGliphToolConfig created by conf_immgliph().

docs.title: Value
docs.text: conf_immgliph() returns a read-only ImmGliphToolConfig. tool_immgliph() returns a reusable ImmGliphTool.

docs.title: Input to tool$run()
docs.text:
tool$run() accepts one immundata::ImmunData dataset. It does not accept a text file directly. The dataset must contain TRB receptors. For paired TRA/TRB data, only the TRB chain is used.

cdr3_col must name a column containing TRB CDR3 amino-acid sequences. Missing and empty CDR3 values are skipped. The other input columns are optional: set v_gene_col, patient_col, hla_col, or counts_col only when the analysis should use those data. Every selected column must exist in the ImmunData dataset.

docs.title: Output from tool$run()
docs.text:
tool$run() returns an ImmGliphRun. It records where the results were saved. To read the result tables, first run results \<- run$results().

ImmGliphResults provides:

  • results$groups: One row for each receptor assigned to a group. The immgliph_group_id column gives the group. Receptors without a group are absent. Use dplyr::collect() to read the table into R.
  • results$connections: Sequence pairs connected by ImmGLIPH and the reason for each connection.
  • results$cluster_properties: One row per group with the properties and scores calculated by ImmGLIPH.
  • results$mapping: The receptor columns that were passed to ImmGLIPH.
  • results$raw_output: Path to the original ImmGLIPH .rds file.
  • results$annotate(idata): A new ImmunData dataset with an immgliph_group_id receptor column. Receptors without a group have NA.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immundapter")


input_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "tcrdist3", "tcr-cluster-simple.tsv",
  package = "immundapter"
)
idata <- immundata::read_repertoires(
  path = input_file,
  schema = immundata::make_receptor_schema(
    features = c("v_call", "j_call", "junction_aa"), chains = "TRB"
  ),
  barcode_col = "cell_id", locus_col = "locus",
  umi_col = "duplicate_count",
  output_folder = tempfile("immgliph-immundata-")
)
config <- conf_immgliph(
  v_gene_col = "v_call",
  n_cores = 4L,
  seed = 1L
)
tool <- tool_immgliph(config)
tool$help()

if (tool$check()) {
  run <- tool$run(idata, output_dir = tempfile("immgliph-run-"))
  results <- run$results()

  groups <- dplyr::collect(results$groups)
  group_scores <- dplyr::collect(results$cluster_properties)
  grouped_idata <- results$annotate(idata)
}

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
RAxML-NG builds a phylogenetic tree for each sequence family. This tool takes aligned nucleotide sequences from immundata::ImmunData and runs each family independently. It does not define families, align sequences, or reconstruct germlines. Complete those steps before running RAxML-NG.

RaxmlNgToolConfig stores validated settings for one type of family-level RAxML-NG analysis. It contains no sequences and no trees. Create it with conf_raxml_ng() and pass it to tool_raxml_ng(). The settings cannot be changed after creation; call conf_raxml_ng() again to use different settings.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
conf_raxml_ng(
  alignment_col = "clone_sequence_alignment",
  family_col = "clone_id",
  tip_col = immundata::imd_schema("receptor"),
  locus = "IGH",
  analysis = c("search", "fast"),
  model = "GTR+G",
  seed = NULL,
  threads = NULL,
  ancestral = FALSE,
  partition_col = NULL,
  brlen = NULL
)

tool_raxml_ng(config = conf_raxml_ng())

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: alignment_col Name of the column containing the aligned nucleotide sequence for each tree tip. This is not IgBLAST’s AIRR sequence_alignment field, which aligns each sequence to a germline rather than to the other sequences in its family. family_col Column containing B-cell clone, lineage, or family names or numbers. Each value is analyzed independently. tip_col Name of the column containing the sequence name used at each tree tip. The default is the ImmunData receptor ID column. locus Receptor locus to use. It must agree with the receptor chains declared by the ImmunData schema. analysis Tree-inference mode. “search” performs the standard maximum-likelihood search; “fast” performs the faster search. model Non-empty RAxML-NG nucleotide model string. The same model is used for every partition in a partitioned analysis. seed Optional positive integer random seed. NULL retains the RAxML-NG default. threads Optional positive integer thread count. NULL retains the RAxML-NG automatic default. ancestral Whether to run RAxML-NG ancestral-state reconstruction on every successfully inferred family tree. partition_col Optional column containing one partition specification per family. brlen Optional branch-length linkage mode: “linked”, “scaled”, or “unlinked”. This setting requires partition_col; partitioned runs default to “scaled”. config A RaxmlNgToolConfig created by conf_raxml_ng().

docs.title: Value
docs.text: conf_raxml_ng() returns a read-only RaxmlNgToolConfig. tool_raxml_ng() returns a reusable RaxmlNgTool.

docs.title: Input to tool$run()
docs.text:
tool$run() accepts one immundata::ImmunData dataset. It does not accept a FASTA file directly. The dataset must contain three columns:

  • family_col: Clone, lineage, or family name. A separate tree is built for each value in this column.
  • tip_col: Sequence name shown at the tips, or leaves, of the tree. Each sequence within a family must have a different name.
  • alignment_col: Aligned nucleotide sequence. All sequences in one family must have the same length.

All three values must be present and non-empty. Repeated rows with the same family, tip, and aligned sequence are used once. A tip cannot have two different sequences in the same family.

additional_tips optionally supplies backend-only tips that are appended after the observed tips are extracted. It must be a data frame or duckplyr table with family_id, tip_id, and aligned_sequence columns. Its family values must already occur in the extracted input. In a partitioned analysis, an optional partition_spec column must agree with the observed family specification; when omitted, that specification is inherited. Additional tips are never added to or joined into ImmunData.

outgroups optionally identifies one or more existing tips per family. It must be a data frame or duckplyr table with family_id and tip_id columns. The identified tips may come from ImmunData or additional_tips. RAxML-NG output is rooted by the adapter, which writes a rooted copy of each successful tree while preserving the raw RAxML-NG tree.

locus selects the receptor chain used for the tree. With paired receptors, only the selected chain is used. The selected locus must agree with the chains stored in the ImmunData dataset.

If partition_col is set, it must contain one consistent partition specification per family in the form name=start-end, with partitions separated by semicolons. For example, IGH=1-300;IGK=301-540 covers a 540-site alignment. Partitions must be unique, non-overlapping, and cover every alignment site.

docs.title: Analysis modes
docs.text:
The tool supports two RAxML-NG tree-inference commands:

  • “search”: Standard maximum-likelihood tree search.
  • “fast”: Faster tree search.

Set ancestral = TRUE to run RAxML-NG ancestral-state reconstruction after each successful family tree. This produces a node-labelled tree, reconstructed internal-node sequences, and marginal state probabilities. A failed ancestral stage does not discard the successful family tree. Other modes that use existing trees or produce other types of output, including evaluate, bootstrap, and support, are not part of this tool. The default nucleotide model is GTR+G. Set seed and threads for reproducible execution, or omit them to retain RAxML-NG’s defaults. Partitioned analyses default to scaled branch-length linkage.

docs.title: Output from tool$run()
docs.text:
tool$run() returns a RaxmlNgRun. It records where the results were saved. To read the trees, first run results \<- run$results().

RaxmlNgResults provides:

  • results$families: One row per family, showing whether the analysis succeeded and where its files were saved. Use dplyr::collect() to read the table into R.
  • results$tree_index: The families that produced a tree and the path to each tree file.
  • results$failed_families: Families that failed, with their exit status and diagnostic message.
  • results$tip_map: The original value from tip_col and the shorter tip label used in the RAxML-NG files.
  • results$outgroups: The original and internal outgroup tip names.
  • results$ancestral_index: Paths to successful ancestral-state files.
  • results$failed_ancestral: Families whose optional ancestral stage failed, with diagnostics.
  • results$read_trees(): One Newick tree per family, returned as a named character vector. When outgroups were supplied, these are rooted copies.
  • results$read_ancestral_trees(): Node-labelled ancestral trees.
  • results$read_ancestral_states(): A duckplyr table of reconstructed internal-node sequences.

Tree files remain in the run directory. Trees cannot be added as columns to ImmunData. Use $read_trees(), $tree_index, or $tip_map for downstream phylogenetic analysis.

Each family has its own directory containing the prepared FASTA file, optional partition file, RAxML-NG output, and log files. A failed family does not discard successful results. The returned run has status “partial” when one or more tree or requested ancestral stages fail.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immundapter")


sequences <- c(
  "ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGT",
  "ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGA",
  "ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTTCGT",
  "ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTTCGTACGT"
)
input_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
utils::write.table(data.frame(
  cell_id = paste0("cell-", seq_along(sequences)),
  locus = "IGH", sequence = sequences, clone_id = "family-a",
  clone_sequence_alignment = sequences, duplicate_count = 1L
), input_file, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
idata <- immundata::read_repertoires(
  path = input_file,
  schema = immundata::make_receptor_schema(
    features = "sequence", chains = "IGH"
  ),
  barcode_col = "cell_id", locus_col = "locus",
  umi_col = "duplicate_count", repertoire_schema = NULL,
  preprocess = NULL, postprocess = NULL, rename_columns = NULL,
  output_folder = tempfile("raxml-immundata-")
)
config <- conf_raxml_ng(
  alignment_col = "clone_sequence_alignment",
  family_col = "clone_id",
  analysis = "search"
)
tool <- tool_raxml_ng(config)
tool$check()

run <- tool$run(idata, output_dir = tempfile("raxml-ng-run-"))
results <- run$results()
dplyr::collect(results$tree_index)
trees <- results$read_trees()

docs.title: Assign germline genes to raw receptor sequences with IgBLAST
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
IgBLAST identifies the germline genes that most likely produced each immune receptor sequence. It produces V, D, J, and, when available, C gene calls in an AIRR table that can be imported with immundata::read_repertoires().

The usual workflow is:

run <- tool_igblast()$run(c(
  fasta = "sequences.fasta",
  annotations = "contig_annotations.csv"
))
idata <- immundata::read_repertoires(
  path = run$results()$final_output,
  schema = immundata::make_receptor_schema(
    features = c("v_call", "j_call", "junction_aa"),
    chains = c("IGH", "IGK|IGL")
  ),
  barcode_col = "barcode",
  locus_col = "locus",
  umi_col = "umis",
  preprocess = immundata::make_default_preprocessing("10x"),
  rename_columns = NULL
)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
conf_igblast(num_threads = NULL, run_args = list())

tool_igblast(config = conf_igblast())

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: num_threads Number of computer threads available to IgBLAST. NULL uses the IgBLAST default. run_args Additional named arguments passed through … in igblastr::igblastn(). This is intended for advanced settings. Arguments required by the immundapter workflow cannot be changed here. config Settings created by conf_igblast().

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
IgBLAST compares observed receptor sequences with a germline database. The database selected through igblastr determines the species and receptor type. For example, select a human BCR database before analysing human immunoglobulin sequences.

Query sequences must be nucleotide sequences without alignment gaps. Supply the complete assembled V(D)J sequence when possible. Amino-acid sequences and sequences that already contain IMGT dots are not valid input. A CDR3 nucleotide sequence alone usually does not contain enough information for useful V- and J-gene annotation.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: conf_igblast() returns read-only IgBLAST settings. tool_igblast() returns a reusable IgBLAST tool.

docs.title: Before the first analysis
docs.text:
Install IgBLAST and one germline database with igblastr. Select the database in the same R session in which you run the analysis:

igblastr::install_igblast()
igblastr::install_IMGT_germline_db(
  "<release>",
  organism = "Homo sapiens",
  tcr.db = FALSE
)
igblastr::use_germline_db("<db-name>")

Use tool$help() for setup commands and tool$check() to confirm that the selected database and IgBLAST installation are ready.

docs.title: Run the tool
docs.text:
tool_igblast() creates a reusable tool. Its main methods are:

  • tool$help(): print installation and database setup instructions;
  • tool$check(): check that IgBLAST and a germline database are ready;
  • tool$run(input, config = NULL, output_dir = NULL): run one analysis.

The tool keeps its default settings in tool$config. Supplying config to $run() replaces those settings for that run only.

docs.title: Choose the input
docs.text:
tool$run() accepts two forms of input:

  • A FASTA file. Pass a path ending in .fasta or .fasta.gz. Use this when no annotation table needs to be preserved.
  • A FASTA file and its annotation table. Pass c(fasta = “sequences.fasta”, annotations = “annotations.csv”). Use this for data such as 10x contigs when barcodes, UMI counts, and sample columns must remain beside the new IgBLAST annotations.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
tool$run() saves the analysis and returns a completed run object. Its $path is the output directory and $artifacts lists the saved files. Call run$results() to access the biological results. Every run provides:

  • results$airr: the complete AIRR annotation table;
  • results$mapping: the link between input records and AIRR sequence_id;
  • results$raw_output: the path to the saved AIRR TSV file.

The tables are disk-backed. Use dplyr::collect() only when you want to bring a table into R memory.

With paired FASTA and annotation input, results$final contains the source columns joined with all AIRR columns. results$final_output is the path to the same table as a TSV file. Pass this file to immundata::read_repertoires() to create an ImmunData dataset. Choose preprocessing that retains sequence_alignment when subsequent analyses need IMGT-gapped alignments and coordinates.

docs.title: IMGT gaps and coordinates
docs.text:
igblastr builds the searchable IgBLAST database from ungapped germline sequences. It also keeps the original IMGT-gapped V references. These two forms have different V-gene coordinates.

For a selected IMGT database, immundapter automatically uses both forms from the same installed database release. IgBLAST first performs the search against the ungapped database. immundapter then uses the matching gapped V allele to place IMGT dots in sequence_alignment and convert v_germline_start and v_germline_end to the IMGT-gapped coordinate system. This follows the normalization used by Change-O for germline reconstruction.

Do not download a newer gapped FASTA separately: allele content and gap positions must match the database used by IgBLAST. If the selected IMGT database does not contain its original gapped V FASTA files, reinstall that database with igblastr::install_IMGT_germline_db().

Normalization uses the first allele in v_call. If the allele or the exact aligned V end cannot be matched to the selected reference, that row keeps the original IgBLAST alignment and coordinates. Non-IMGT databases are also returned in their original IgBLAST coordinate system. D- and J-region coordinates are not converted to IMGT-gapped V coordinates.

docs.title: Input details
docs.text: FASTA names must be unique. In >cell_1 description, the name is cell_1. For paired input, the annotation table must contain a unique contig_id or sequence_id column whose values match the FASTA names. CSV, TSV, TXT, and gzip-compressed annotation files are accepted.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: igblastr overview

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immundapter")


# Select an installed human BCR IMGT database.
databases <- igblastr::list_germline_dbs(names.only = TRUE)
databases <- grep(
  "Homo_sapiens.IGH+IGK+IGL",
  databases,
  value = TRUE,
  fixed = TRUE
)
databases <- grep("^IMGT-", databases, value = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(databases) > 0L)
suppressMessages(
  igblastr::use_germline_db(sort(databases)[[length(databases)]])
)

config <- conf_igblast()
tool <- tool_igblast(config)
stopifnot(tool$check())

antitnf_dir <- system.file("extdata", "antitnf", package = "immundapter")
antitnf_fasta <- file.path(antitnf_dir, "bcr_contigs.fasta.gz")
antitnf_annotations <- file.path(
  antitnf_dir,
  "contig_annotations.csv.gz"
)

# Analyse a FASTA file directly.
fasta_run <- tool$run(
  antitnf_fasta,
  output_dir = tempfile("igblast-fasta-")
)
fasta_airr <- dplyr::collect(fasta_run$results()$airr)

# Preserve the matching 10x annotation table and import the AIRR result.
paired_run <- tool$run(
  c(
    fasta = antitnf_fasta,
    annotations = antitnf_annotations
  ),
  output_dir = tempfile("igblast-10x-")
)
idata <- immundata::read_repertoires(
  path = paired_run$results()$final_output,
  schema = immundata::make_receptor_schema(
    features = c("v_call", "j_call", "junction_aa"),
    chains = c("IGH", "IGK|IGL")
  ),
  barcode_col = "barcode",
  locus_col = "locus",
  umi_col = "umis",
  preprocess = immundata::make_default_preprocessing("10x"),
  rename_columns = NULL,
  output_folder = tempfile("antitnf-immundata-")
)

docs.title: Compare and group T-cell receptors with tcrdist3
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
tcrdist3 measures how similar T-cell receptors are from their CDR3 amino-acid sequences and V/J genes. A smaller distance means that two receptors are more similar. The tool can return the distances alone or use them to place similar receptors into groups.

The usual workflow is:

tool <- tool_tcrdist3()
run <- tool$run(idata)
results <- run$results()
clusters <- dplyr::collect(results$clusters)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
conf_tcrdist3(
  mode = c("cluster", "distance"),
  organism = "human",
  chains = "beta",
  cdr3_cols = c(beta = "junction_aa"),
  v_gene_cols = c(beta = "v_call"),
  j_gene_cols = c(beta = "j_call"),
  db_file = "alphabeta_gammadelta_db.tsv",
  store_all_cdr = TRUE,
  deduplicate = TRUE,
  cpus = 1L,
  radius = 24L,
  python = NULL,
  run_args = list()
)

tool_tcrdist3(config = conf_tcrdist3())

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: mode “cluster” groups similar receptors and returns their distances. “distance” returns only the distance matrix and its input mapping. organism Species used to interpret V/J genes: “human” or “mouse”. chains One or two chains selected from “alpha”, “beta”, “gamma”, and “delta”. With two chains, their distances are added. cdr3_cols Named vector giving the CDR3 amino-acid column for each selected chain, for example c(beta = “junction_aa”). v_gene_cols Named vector giving the V-gene column for each selected chain. Gene names must be recognized by the tcrdist3 database. j_gene_cols Named vector giving the J-gene column for each selected chain. db_file Germline reference supplied to tcrdist3. The default reference is included with tcrdist3. store_all_cdr Whether to save separate distance matrices for individual receptor regions in addition to the combined matrices. deduplicate Whether to calculate identical receptors once. Results are still reported for every original receptor. cpus Number of CPU cores used by tcrdist3. radius Largest distance that directly connects two receptors during clustering. It is used only when mode = “cluster”. python Python executable name or path. NULL selects the managed tcrdist3 environment described above. run_args Additional named arguments passed to TCRrep. This is for advanced settings. Values must be valid JSON values. Arguments controlled by immundapter cannot be changed here. config Settings created by conf_tcrdist3().

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
tcrdist3 compares receptor sequences; it does not prove that receptors bind the same antigen. Treat the distance and cluster threshold as analysis choices that should be checked for the biological question and dataset.

Every selected chain needs a CDR3 amino-acid sequence, a V-gene call, and a J-gene call. The defaults expect human TRB data stored in junction_aa, v_call, and j_call.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: conf_tcrdist3() returns read-only tcrdist3 settings. tool_tcrdist3() returns a reusable tcrdist3 tool.

docs.title: Choose distances or clusters
docs.text:
Use mode = “cluster”, the default, to calculate distances and group receptors. Two receptors are connected when their distance is at most radius. All receptors connected directly or through other receptors become one cluster. Consequently, two receptors in the same cluster can have a direct distance greater than radius.

Use mode = “distance” when only the pairwise distance matrix is needed. Distance-only results do not contain clusters and cannot be added to ImmunData with $annotate().

docs.title: Choose the receptor chains
docs.text:
chains selects the chains used in the distance:

  • chains = “beta”, the default, compares TRB only. It can select the beta chain from paired TRA/TRB ImmunData.
  • chains = c(“alpha”, “beta”) compares both sides of a paired receptor. tcrdist3 calculates one distance per chain and adds them.

Alpha, beta, gamma, and delta chains are supported. organism must match the gene names in the data. Because paired-chain distances are sums, a radius chosen for one chain should not be assumed to work for two chains.

For paired ImmunData, the receptor schema tells the tool which row belongs to each chain, so both chains can use the same feature names:

conf_tcrdist3(
  chains = c("alpha", "beta"),
  cdr3_cols = c(alpha = "junction_aa", beta = "junction_aa"),
  v_gene_cols = c(alpha = "v_call", beta = "v_call"),
  j_gene_cols = c(alpha = "j_call", beta = "j_call")
)

docs.title: Choose the input
docs.text:
tool$run() accepts:

  • An ImmunData dataset. The selected columns must be receptor features. The tool prepares one row per biological receptor. Cluster results can be added back with results$annotate(idata).
  • A CSV, TSV, or TXT file. Each row must represent one receptor. Paired receptors need separate CDR3, V-gene, and J-gene columns for each chain.

Rows missing a required value for a selected chain are excluded. For text input, imd_receptor_id is used as the identifier when present, followed by cell_id; otherwise, row numbers are used.

docs.title: Run the tool
docs.text:
tool_tcrdist3() creates a reusable tool. Its main methods are:

  • tool$help(): print commands for installing the Python environment;
  • tool$check(): check that Python and tcrdist3 are ready;
  • tool$run(input, config = NULL, output_dir = NULL): run one analysis.

The tool keeps its default settings in tool$config. Supplying config to $run() replaces those settings for that run only. The completed run stores its output directory in $path and its saved files in $artifacts.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
Call run$results() after a successful run. Both modes provide:

  • results$distances: the path to the complete NumPy distance matrix;
  • results$mapping: the link between input receptors and rows of that matrix.

Cluster mode also provides:

  • results$clusters: one cluster number and cluster size per receptor;
  • results$edges: receptor pairs whose distance is at most radius;
  • results$annotate(idata): a new ImmunData dataset containing tcrdist_cluster_id and tcrdist_cluster_size.

Result tables stay on disk and are evaluated with duckplyr. Use dplyr::collect() when a table is small enough to bring into R memory. The distance matrix is a NumPy .npy file, not an R table.

docs.title: Calculation details
docs.text: With deduplicate = TRUE, identical selected receptors are calculated once and then matched back to every original receptor. results$mapping records this relationship. Set store_all_cdr = FALSE when separate region-specific distance matrices are not needed.

docs.title: Python setup
docs.text:
By default, immundapter uses a dedicated Python environment at environments/tcrdist3 under tools::R_user_dir(“immundapter”, “data”). Call tool$help() to print the installation commands and tool$check() to verify the environment. $help() prints instructions; it does not install software.

Set IMMUNDAPTER_DATA before creating the configuration to use another data directory, or supply python to use a specific Python executable.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: immundata::ImmunData, tcrdist3 input, tcrdist3 documentation

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immundapter")


# Group similar TRB receptors in the bundled example.
config <- conf_tcrdist3(
  store_all_cdr = FALSE,
  cpus = 1L,
  radius = 24L
)
tool <- tool_tcrdist3(config)
stopifnot(tool$check())

input_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "tcrdist3", "tcr-cluster-simple.tsv",
  package = "immundapter"
)
run <- tool$run(
  input_file,
  output_dir = tempfile("tcrdist3-file-")
)
results <- run$results()
clusters <- dplyr::collect(results$clusters)

# Add the cluster assignments to ImmunData.
snapshot <- system.file(
  "extdata", "tcrdist3", "immundata-tcr-cluster-simple",
  package = "immundapter"
)
idata <- immundata::read_immundata(snapshot, verbose = FALSE)
idata_run <- tool$run(
  idata,
  output_dir = tempfile("tcrdist3-immundata-")
)
annotated_idata <- idata_run$results()$annotate(idata)

# Calculate distances without creating clusters.
distance_tool <- tool_tcrdist3(conf_tcrdist3(
  mode = "distance", store_all_cdr = FALSE
))
distance_run <- distance_tool$run(
  input_file,
  output_dir = tempfile("tcrdist3-distance-")
)
distance_file <- distance_run$results()$distances
